title: Migrate equestrian e2e to @pm990320/playwright-checkpoint
Publish playwright-checkpoint to npm
description:
Publish the package to npm as `playwright-checkpoint` (unscoped) using trusted publishing.

**⚠️ REQUIRES PATRICK'S EXPLICIT APPROVAL BEFORE PUBLISHING ⚠️**
Do NOT run `npm publish` locally. Publishing happens via GitHub Actions with OIDC trusted publishing.

## Version Strategy
- **First publish:** `0.1.0-beta.1` (npm `beta` dist-tag)
- Users install with: `npm install playwright-checkpoint@beta`
- Promote to stable later: `0.1.0` (npm `latest` dist-tag)

## One-time setup (Patrick to do manually)

### npm side
1. Log in to npmjs.com as `pm990320`
2. Go to package settings for `playwright-checkpoint` (may need to create placeholder first)
3. Publishing access → Trusted Publishing → Add GitHub Actions:
   - Repository: `gecckio/playwright-checkpoint`
   - Environment: `npm`
   - Workflow: `publish.yml`

### GitHub side
1. Go to github.com/gecckio/playwright-checkpoint → Settings → Environments
2. Create environment: `npm`
3. Add yourself as required reviewer (publish gate)

## Publish workflow (already set up in .github/workflows/publish.yml)
Triggered by pushing a `v*` tag. Runs: checkout → install → typecheck → build → test → lint → verify tag matches package.json → `npm publish --provenance --access public`.

Uses OIDC `id-token: write` permission. No npm tokens needed.

## To publish each release
```bash
# 1. Ensure package.json version matches
# 2. Commit
git commit -am "release: v0.1.0-beta.1"
# 3. Tag
git tag v0.1.0-beta.1
# 4. Push
git push && git push --tags
# 5. GitHub Actions handles the rest (approve in environment review)
```

## Pre-publish checklist
- [ ] Package name `playwright-checkpoint` confirmed available (checked 2026-04-03)
- [ ] npm trusted publishing configured (OIDC, gecckio/playwright-checkpoint, npm environment)
- [ ] GitHub `npm` environment created with required reviewer
- [ ] README is polished and accurate
- [ ] All P0/P1 issues closed
- [ ] Version in package.json set to `0.1.0-beta.1`
- [ ] `npm pack` reviewed — no junk files, reasonable size
- [ ] `package.json` fields complete: name, version, description, keywords, repository, license, author, main, types, exports
- [ ] TypeScript declarations included in build output
- [ ] `.github/workflows/publish.yml` present and correct
- [ ] Tag `v0.1.0-beta.1` created and pushed
- [ ] GitHub Actions publish job approved and green

## Reference
Pattern from existing projects:
- `~/git/ultimate-playwright-mcp/.github/workflows/publish.yml`
- `~/git/google-workspace-mcp/.github/workflows/publish.yml`

title: Help article compiler — MDX output format
description:
MDX output format for the help article compiler, enabling interactive documentation sites.

**Why MDX over plain Markdown:**
- Embed React components (image zoom, tabs for device variants, collapsible steps)
- Frontmatter for docs frameworks (Docusaurus, Nextra, Fumadocs, etc.)
- Import checkpoint data as structured props
- Interactive before/after comparisons across checkpoints

**Output per test:**
```mdx
---
title: Sign in to your account
sidebar_label: Sign In
tags: [authentication, onboarding]
---

import { Screenshot } from '@pm990320/playwright-checkpoint/components';
import { StepList, Step } from '@pm990320/playwright-checkpoint/components';

<StepList>
  <Step number={1} title="Navigate to the login page">
    <Screenshot src="./screenshots/login-page.png" alt="Login page" highlight={{x: 120, y: 340, w: 400, h: 200}} />
    Navigate to `/login`. You'll see the login form.
  </Step>
  <Step number={2} title="Enter credentials">
    <Screenshot src="./screenshots/credentials.png" alt="Filled form" />
    Enter your email and password, then click **Sign In**.
  </Step>
</StepList>
```

**Deliverables:**
- MDX template engine alongside existing Markdown compiler
- Optional React component library export (`/components`)
- Frontmatter generation from manifest metadata (title, tags, environment)
- Device variant tabs (desktop/mobile screenshots side by side)
- Format selectable via CLI: `--format mdx`
- Configurable: custom component imports, frontmatter schema

title: Unit tests for collector pipeline and config resolution
description:
Write unit tests for the core checkpoint fixture and collector pipeline.

**Test cases:**
- Config cascade: global defaults → per-test overrides → per-checkpoint overrides merge correctly
- Collector enable/disable: disabled collectors don't run
- Collector execution: each built-in collector produces expected output shape
- Custom collector registration: user-provided collector is called with correct context
- Manifest generation: manifest JSON has correct structure, all checkpoints recorded
- Error handling: collector failure doesn't crash the test (graceful degradation)
- Axe graceful skip: when @axe-core/playwright is not installed, axe collector skips without error
- Checkpoint naming: slug sanitization, duplicate names handled

**Approach:**
- Mock Playwright's Page and TestInfo where needed
- Test collector functions in isolation (they're just async functions)
- Test the pipeline orchestration separately

- Multiple reporters: all configured reporters run and produce output

title: Create OpenClaw agent skill for playwright-checkpoint
description:
Create an OpenClaw/AI agent skill (SKILL.md + references) that teaches agents how to effectively use playwright-checkpoint — not just setup, but the full workflow of writing tests, analyzing outputs, and iterating on issues.

**Location:** Published to clawhub.ai (or local skill under ~/.openclaw/skills/playwright-checkpoint/)

**Installation section (brief):**
- npm install, fixture setup, config, globalTeardown — keep this short, link to README

**Primary focus — the agent workflow:**

### 1. Writing effective e2e tests with checkpointing
- When to place checkpoints (key user journey milestones, not every click)
- Naming conventions for checkpoints (descriptive, ordered: "01-landing", "02-after-login")
- Using `description` and `step` fields for documentation generation
- Using `highlightSelector` to mark the focus element for each step
- Tagging tests: @smoke, @prod-safe, @user-journey, @destructive, @fixtures
- Per-test config for journey-specific collector needs

### 2. The Page Object Model pattern
- Why POM matters for maintainable e2e tests
- Structure: one class per page/component, methods for actions, getters for assertions
- How checkpoints fit into POM (checkpoint in the test, not in the page object)
- Example pattern:
  ```typescript
  test('user signs up', async ({ page, checkpoint }) => {
    const signup = new SignupPage(page);
    await signup.open();
    await checkpoint('signup form', { highlightSelector: '[data-testid="signup-form"]' });
    await signup.fillEmail('test@example.com');
    await signup.fillPassword('secure123');
    await signup.submit();
    await checkpoint('after signup submit');
    const dashboard = new DashboardPage(page);
    await dashboard.expectWelcomeMessage();
    await checkpoint('dashboard loaded');
  });
  ```

### 3. Analyzing checkpoint outputs to find issues
This is the core skill — teaching the agent to be a QA analyst.

**Reading the checkpoint manifest:**
- Structure of checkpoint-manifest.json
- How to correlate checkpoints across device variants (desktop-light, mobile-dark, etc.)
- Identifying which checkpoints failed or have issues

**Analyzing specific collector outputs:**
- **Screenshots:** Compare across variants — look for layout breaks, overflow, missing elements on mobile
- **Axe results:** How to read axe.json, prioritize violations (critical > serious > moderate), common fixes
- **Web Vitals:** What good/needs-improvement/poor means for each metric, how to diagnose LCP/CLS/INP issues
- **Console errors:** Filtering noise vs real errors, correlating with page state
- **Failed requests:** 404s, CORS issues, API failures — what they mean in context
- **Metadata:** SEO issues (missing og:tags, wrong lang, missing canonical)
- **HTML snapshots:** DOM analysis for structure issues, missing ARIA attributes

**The triage workflow:**
1. Run tests → read manifest summary
2. Identify failing/degraded checkpoints
3. Deep-dive: open specific collector artifacts
4. Correlate across collectors (e.g., high CLS + layout-shift in screenshot)
5. Formulate diagnosis and fix
6. Re-run specific test to verify fix

### 4. Narrowing in on specific flows/issues
- How to run a single test: `npx playwright test path/to/test.spec.ts`
- How to run a single project variant: `--project mobile-dark`
- How to grep for tags: `--grep @payments`
- Using the HTML report to visually compare checkpoints
- Using `checkpoint()` options to enable extra collectors for debugging
- Adding temporary checkpoints to bisect a flow

### 5. Common patterns and anti-patterns

**Good patterns:**
- Checkpoint at stable states (page fully loaded, animation complete)
- Use `settlePage()` behavior — don't checkpoint during transitions
- One test = one user journey
- Clean test data (fixtures, not shared state)
- Descriptive checkpoint names that read as documentation

**Anti-patterns:**
- Checkpointing after every action (too much noise)
- Brittle selectors (prefer data-testid, roles, text)
- Tests that depend on each other
- Ignoring axe violations ("we'll fix a11y later")
- Not testing mobile variants

### 6. Generating and using help articles
- How to add descriptions/steps for doc generation
- Running the article compiler
- Reviewing and editing generated articles
- Keeping articles in sync with test changes

**Skill structure:**
```
playwright-checkpoint/
  SKILL.md                    # Main skill file
  references/
    checkpoint-manifest.md    # Manifest schema reference
    collector-outputs.md      # What each collector produces
    workflow-examples.md      # Step-by-step triage examples
    page-object-patterns.md   # POM examples and patterns
```

**Tone:** Practical, workflow-oriented. The agent should feel like a senior QA engineer who knows exactly what to look at and in what order.

**Current state:**

5. Keep beforeEach hook (startup status, theme, cookie consent, stripe) as-is
6. Delete `e2e/support/checkpoint-report.ts` — replaced by package
7. Delete `e2e/support/device-profile.ts` — replaced by package
8. Update `e2e/global-teardown.ts` to use package's teardown or import
9. Delete `e2e/scripts/generate-checkpoint-report.ts` — use package CLI
10. Run full test suite — verify all 4 project variants pass
11. Verify checkpoint report HTML output matches previous quality
12. Verify all checkpoint artifacts still attach to Playwright HTML report
